A child with a squint isn't just looking different. Their brain may be switching one eye off.
Stay till the end, because there's a deadline most parents don't know about.
Your brain builds one picture from two eyes. When the eyes point in different directions, it sees double.
So a young brain does something clever, and dangerous. It starts ignoring the turned eye.
But if that goes on, the ignored eye stops developing good vision. This is called lazy eye, or amblyopia.
Wait, can it be fixed? Yes. Treatment works best in early childhood, while the brain's vision wiring is still flexible.
That's why a squint after four months of age is not something to wait out. Get it checked by an eye doctor.
